title: Butein inhibits cancer cell growth by rescuing the wild-type thermal stability of mutant p53.
authors: Song, Bin; Wang, Jiajian; Ren, Yixin; Su, Yongnan; Geng, Xueye; Yang, Fan; Wang, Hao; Zhang, Jihong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子Butein通过变构机制恢复突变p53的DNA结合能力与热稳定性，涉及TF-DNA互作但以实验为主，仅含简单对接，方法深度有限。
abstract: p53 is a transcription factor that activates the expression of various genes involved in the maintenance of genomic stability, and more than 50% of cancers harbor inactivating p53 mutations, which are indicative of highly aggressive cancer and poor prognosis. Pharmacological targeting of mutant p53 to restore the wild-type p53 tumor-suppressing function is a promising strategy for cancer therapy. In this study, we identified a small molecule, Butein, that reactivates mutant p53 activity in tumor cells harboring the R175H or R273H mutation. Butein restored wild-type-like conformation and DNA-binding ability in HT29 and SK-BR-3 cells harboring mutant p53-R175H and mutant p53-R273H, respectively. Moreover, Butein enabled the transactivation of p53 target genes and decreased the interactions of Hsp90 with mutant p53-R175H and mutant p53-R273H proteins, while Hsp90 overexpression reversed targeted p53 gene activation. In addition, Butein induced thermal stabilization of wild-type p53, mutant p53-R273H and mutant p53-R175H, as determined via CETSA. From docking study, we further proved that Butein binding to p53 stabilized the DNA-binding loop-sheet-helix motif of mutant p53-R175H and regulated its DNA-binding activity via an allosteric mechanism, conferring wild-type-like the DNA-binding activity of mutant p53. Collectively, the data suggest that Butein is a potential antitumor agent that restores p53 function in cancers harboring mutant p53-R273H or mutant p53-R175H. SIGNIFICANCE: Butein restores the ability of mutant p53 to bind DNA by reversing its transition to the Loop3 (L3) state, endows p53 mutants with thermal stability and re-establishes their transcriptional activity to induce cancer cell death.
abstract_zh: p53是一种转录因子，激活参与基因组稳定性维持的各种基因表达，超过50%的癌症携带失活的p53突变，这些突变预示着高度侵袭性癌症和不良预后。通过药理学靶向突变型p53以恢复野生型p53的肿瘤抑制功能，是癌症治疗的一种有前景的策略。在本研究中，我们鉴定了一种小分子Butein，它能在携带R175H或R273H突变的肿瘤细胞中重新激活突变型p53的活性。Butein分别在携带突变型p53-R175H和突变型p53-R273H的HT29和SK-BR-3细胞中恢复了类似野生型的构象和DNA结合能力。此外，Butein使p53靶基因的反式激活成为可能，并减少了Hsp90与突变型p53-R175H和突变型p53-R273H蛋白的相互作用，而Hsp90过表达则逆转了靶向p53基因的激活。另外，通过CETSA测定，Butein诱导了野生型p53、突变型p53-R273H和突变型p53-R175H的热稳定性。通过对接研究，我们进一步证明Butein与p53的结合稳定了突变型p53-R175H的DNA结合环-片层-螺旋基序，并通过变构机制调节其DNA结合活性，赋予突变型p53类似野生型的DNA结合活性。综合来看，数据表明Butein是一种潜在的抗肿瘤剂，能在携带突变型p53-R273H或突变型p53-R175H的癌症中恢复p53功能。意义：Butein通过逆转突变型p53向Loop3 (L3)状态的转变，恢复其DNA结合能力，赋予p53突变体热稳定性，并重新建立其转录活性以诱导癌细胞死亡。
